summary: Oconee County, SC tower in Sumter National Forest, built about 1935 for the Forest Service and NHLR-registered in 2013; current access not confirmed.

facts.design: 54' Aermotor LS-40 tower with 7'x7' metal cab, low hip roof and atypical window configuration
facts.status_note: Last described as standing in a 2020 blog post; no newer report found

staffing.status: used by the Forest Service until the 1980s; no lookouts named in the sources read

access.note: On Sumter National Forest land; no Forest Service page was checked for climbing or access. A 2020 blog writer entered the cab and found the tower open probably by mistake.

visit.trail_note: Off South Carolina Highway 107 in an isolated spot, per a 2020 blog; no official visit information found. Do not climb without Forest Service confirmation.

notes_for_editor: Register and one 2020 blog visit are the only sources read. Height converted from the register's 54 ft. Register says the Forest Service used the tower until the 1980s; no exact year, so no staffing event was recorded. Access and climbing status are unconfirmed; no Forest Service page was checked for closure notices. The brief's standing status rests on the 2020 blog and the register. The OpenStreetMap node (height 16.5) agrees but is not cited. Story does not encourage climbing.
